observations: Torah #124 contains no bechina language whatsoever. It is a brief practical teaching (hanhaga/advice) about remaining in the place where hirhurei teshuva and histokekut arise, without moving. All relationships between concepts are causal/practical (eitza): inspiration arrives -> express it immediately -> do not move -> or it may cease. Without any bechina-connected concepts, no packages (existing or new) can be formed. The teaching's concepts (hirhurei teshuva, histokekut, makom, diburim shel techinot) could potentially appear as nodes in eitza chains connecting to packages in other torahs, but they do not form a bechina-based cluster here.
